leads.title: WSFS, F.S.B. v. Wahl, III and Brookside Properties, LLC (Confession of Judgment on $6M Commercial Guaranty Affirmed)
leads.why: Delaware Superior Court (Nov. 18, 2026) adopted a Commissioner's findings and affirmed that confession-of-judgment provisions in commercial guaranties signed by H. Adam Wahl, III and his company Brookside Properties, LLC are valid and enforceable, rejecting the guarantors' due-process waiver challenge after two evidentiary hearings. Brookside owned the commercial property (a fabrication shop) it leased to Quality Heating and Air-Conditioning, Inc., the $6,000,000 WSFS borrower that defaulted; Wahl and Brookside guaranteed the loan. Matters to CRE lenders and guarantors because it confirms Delaware courts will enforce confession-of-judgment clauses in commercial guaranties against both individual and LLC guarantors, letting a lender obtain judgment without a full merits trial.

leads.title: EPIC Companies Midwest, LLC v. HI West Acres, LLC (fka EPIC Hospitality) -- North Dakota bankruptcy adversary trial
leads.why: A jury trial began October 6, 2026 in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of North Dakota (Judge Peter Welte) in an adversary proceeding inside EPIC Companies Midwest's Chapter 11 case: EPIC Companies Midwest and EOLA Capital sued HI West Acres, LLC (formerly EPIC Hospitality, LLC) over roughly $900,000 tied to real estate development project financing. Flagged for the newsroom's own freshness judgment: this is the sole North Dakota candidate found this run (the tracker has zero ND matters), but the only coverage is six weeks old with no outcome/verdict reported yet despite a follow-up search.

leads.title: 73 Dun One, Inc. v. Gould Holdings, LLC (NJ Appellate Division affirms loss of commercial lease right-of-first-refusal claim)
leads.why: New Jersey Appellate Division (Nov. 19, 2026) affirmed summary judgment against a longtime commercial tenant (operating a franchise location in Berlin Township, NJ) that sued the property owners/estate and the buyer, Gould Holdings, LLC, claiming it was denied its lease's contractual right of first refusal when the property was sold; the court remanded only on a separate dispute over the real estate tax amount owed under the lease. Relevant to CRE landlords, tenants and buyers on how courts read ROFR clauses in long-term commercial leases against estate/trust ownership transitions and sales to related buyers.

leads.title: Bridgewater Commons (NJ) $235M CMBS Loan Moves to Special Servicing
leads.why: Commercial Observer (Nov. 2026, citing Morningstar Credit) reports the $235M CMBS loan on Bridgewater Commons, a 1.15M-sq-ft New Jersey mall sponsored by Pacific Retail Capital Partners, moved to special servicing after missing a 9.25% debt yield hurdle at its extended maturity, despite a $3.4M curtailment and an April 2026 parcel sale that raised $54.3M to pay down the loan; relevant to CRE lenders and special servicers as a likely precursor to foreclosure litigation on a single-asset, single-borrower CMBS deal (GSMS 2012-BWTR). Not yet a lawsuit -- newsroom should judge whether to write this as a distress/workout item or wait for a filing.
